ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure is a circuit diagram, with a battery labeled 12 volts on the left; the battery is connected through a resistor labeled 50 Ω to the terminal area on the right; on the right there is a Zener diode labeled Zener diode, and there is also a Motor, the two are connected between the same controlled node and the return terminal, forming a parallel load structure. Reasoning: The problem gives that the battery voltage remains 12 V, the Zener diode is 5 V, and the motor current I_motor = 90 mA. Since the 5 V Zener diode clamps the parallel node, the voltage of the motor/Zener branch is 5 V. The voltage across the series 50 Ω resistor is 12 V - 5 V = 7 V, so the resistor current is I_R = 7 V / 50 Ω = 0.14 A = 140 mA. According to conservation of node current, the Zener current I_zener = 140 mA - 90 mA = 50 mA. The Zener power P_zener = V_zener × I_zener = 5 V × 50 mA = 250 mW.

method.method_draft: From the image, identify the 50 Ω resistor in series between the 12 V battery and the parallel motor/zener branch. From the text, take Vbattery = 12 V, Vz = 5 V, and Imotor = 90 mA. Since the zener clamps the motor node at 5 V, the resistor voltage is 12 − 5 = 7 V, so its current is 7/50 = 0.14 A = 140 mA. By KCL, Izener = 140 mA − 90 mA = 50 mA. Therefore Pzener = 5 V × 50 mA = 250 mW.
